Hi Maya / Tessa,

Quick finance confirmation from Redwood: for IRS TIN-matching and 1099-NEC reporting we need the legal name on the W-9 to match the name associated with the EIN in IRS records. A DBA on the invoice is fine for payment processing, but our tax/1099 practice requires that vendor records contain the true legal entity name. If the W-9 you have lists a DBA only, we cannot use that as sole proof for year-end reporting.

Acceptable evidence to clear the invoice and proceed with payment:
- A corrected, signed W-9 showing the legal name "Redwood Inference, Inc." and the EIN, OR
- A signed W-9 plus one of the following: IRS CP575 (EIN confirmation letter), a bank letter referencing the EIN and legal name, or articles of incorporation/organization showing the legal name + EIN.

If Cloudbound would prefer to proceed immediately, we can accept payment to the DBA for the wire and then update vendor records once we receive corrected docs — but we would need a written AP authorization (DocuSign OK) from Cloudbound stating you accept the DBA for payment and will not hold Redwood liable for 1099 discrepancies. I can send a short authorization template if helpful.

Next steps I propose: 1) Maya — send corrected W-9 or the CP575 copy; or 2) If you need payment released before we receive corrected docs, reply-all with an AP authorization and I’ll mark AP ticket AP-2247 for manual exception.
